chapter: Regional bands, politics and travel abroad
title: Reception abroad in South Africa and Ireland
summary: Wilson says audiences in South Africa and Ireland were as enthusiastic as anywhere, with music overcoming politics.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: And we see that so well in music, Ted, look at how you've been to every place you can possibly name -- how were you received as a musician, not as a black musician, but as a musician.
People understood, this is a language and the language of music.
How were you received in South Africa?

Oh, as good a reception as I ever had in any part of the world. The enthusiasm of South Africa just like the enthusiasm in Ireland, too. For some reason, the emotional enthusiasm of the jazz fans in Ireland exceeds anything that I have seen -- people kissed my hands like I was a Pope or something. Those fans.
And they were sincere, too. But that South Africa thing, this overcomes all that political
